title: Quarterly plan: Dedicated capacity strategy and autoscaling mechanics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Define a practical quarterly roadmap that aligns Dedicated capacity commitments, autoscaling mechanics, and product SLAs to reduce customer cost variability while preserving latency SLOs. Scope: 1) Design two-tier autoscale behavior (reserved steady-state + burst pool) including policies for preemptible capacity, warm VMs, and KV cache priming; 2) Productize customer-facing controls in Console for autoscale policy, burst caps, and failover routing; 3) Establish rollout plan and metrics for canary and GA across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments. Out of scope for this quarter: deep kernel/runtime rework and new quantization profiles (deferred to runtime-1.20).
updates: 2025-01-08: Kickoff with infra, runtime, and sales engineering. Agreed north star: 99th pct latency < 120ms for steady-state + bounded tail in burst scenarios.

2025-01-22: Cost model first pass completed — shows potential 18-26% unit-cost reduction for typical batchy workloads when autoscale uses warm pool + prefix caching. Shared spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/drive-autoscale-cost-model

2025-02-03: Trade-off discussion: aggressive warm pool sizing reduces cold-start latency but increases committed spend. Decided on conservative defaults with customer opt-in for higher warm-capacity tiers.

2025-02-10: Design review with Runtime and Console teams. Action items: (a) runtime API extension for warm-pool reservation (ENG ticket assigned), (b) Console UX mockups for autoscale policy and burst budget, (c) Add telemetry hooks for prefix-KV cache hit rates.

2025-02-14: Sales engineering flagged prioritized customers (3 enterprise pilots) that require hard SLAs for failover; added requirement for immediate fallback to compatible model variants when capacity constrained.
2025-02-19: Finalized quarter milestones and acceptance criteria. PRD published: https://confluence.company.com/display/INF/PM-7932+-+Dedicated+Autoscale+Quarterly+Plan
acceptance_criteria: PRD approved by Eng, Runtime, and Console leads
Console UI: customers can set steady-state capacity, burst cap, and warm-pool tier in a single flow
Runtime: API to reserve warm capacity and an endpoint to query current warm vs burst pool utilization
Telemetry: dashboards showing steady vs burst token percentages, KV cache hit rate, cold-start latency distribution
Cost model validated against 3 pilot customers with <10% variance vs expected savings
Canary rollout plan documented with rollback criteria and SLO guardrails
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Warm pool increases committed spend and may be unpopular with cost-sensitive customers -> Mitigation: conservative defaults + opt-in higher tiers + clear cost/latency tradeoff UI
Risk: KV cache priming during bursts could be slow on first requests -> Mitigation: priming prewarm for identified prefixes and instrumentation to detect low hit-rate scenarios
Risk: Autoscale complexity increases support burden -> Mitigation: ship with guided presets and diagnostics view for support engineers
Risk: Failure modes when warm pool is exhausted -> Mitigation: automated fallback to compatible smaller model variants and throttling policy with descriptive errors
milestones: Milestone 1 (2025-01-31): PRD + cost model + pilot customer list finalized
Milestone 2 (2025-02-28): Runtime API + Console mockups + telemetry schema committed
Milestone 3 (2025-03-20): Internal canary with two pilot customers; iterate on defaults
Milestone 4 (2025-03-31): GA readiness checklist complete and rollout plan scheduled
